text_and_structure_comparison.current_output_basis: A fictional sample generated from RentalCaseModel and DocumentGenerator at baseline commit 1cb15822aa50f3b9708e649c212057b327c2ed6d; no real case data was used.

text_and_structure_comparison.summary: The current output is a narrative, lessor-oriented complaint. Core arrears claims and facts are covered. The official element table adds party detail, claim items, jurisdiction and preservation sections, fact elements and a mediation-preference section that the current model does not capture. The comparison records 35 open gaps; none is approved for implementation.
highest_priority_open_questions: Whether the product should remain a lessor-only arrears template or also support a lessee plaintiff (delivery of premises and deposit return).
Whether an already-terminated lease requires a claim confirming the termination date.
Whether return of the premises and damages for termination must be separate claims.
Whether the official element-table style should be adopted, or the current narrative pleading style retained with selected elements added.

findings.title: Partial payment is followed by a blanket non-payment statement
findings.evidence: Sample A records a partial payment of 1500 on 2026-04-20 and then states '但被告至今未支付' in the same fact paragraph.
findings.recommended_action: Generate the non-payment statement from a user-confirmed as-of date and outstanding balance; allow partial payment, settlement and set-off; do not append a blanket non-payment assertion.
findings.fix_evidence: RentalCaseModel now derives the payment sentence from the required payment-status classification. Partial payment emits '已支付部分租金，尚欠上述金额' and never '至今未支付'; unknown emits a neutral reconciliation sentence. Tests: test_partial_payment_does_not_append_blanket_non_payment, test_unpaid_payment_status_adds_an_explicit_statement, test_unknown_payment_status_defers_to_reconciliation.

findings.title: Multiple defendants' signing capacity and payment obligations are not separated
findings.evidence: Sample A lists a company defendant and a natural-person defendant, but the facts state that the plaintiff and '被告' signed the contract and the claims direct payment by '被告' without identifying which defendant signed or owes which amount.
findings.recommended_action: Capture each defendant's role, signing capacity and obligation; render them separately or consolidate only after user confirmation.
findings.fix_evidence: RentalCaseModel now detects multiple named defendants and renders claims/facts against each defendant's contractual obligation. The rental page requires a multi-defendant identity and payment-obligation description before completion. Tests: test_multiple_defendants_use_obligation_based_wording, test_multiple_defendants_require_obligation_description.

findings.title: Default evidence suggestions are exported as confirmed evidence with an '原件核对' note
findings.evidence: Sample A's evidence list contains five default suggestions and adds '原件核对' to every row, including a termination/return evidence item that may not exist.
findings.recommended_action: Distinguish suggested rows from user-confirmed evidence; export only confirmed items; do not add '原件核对' by default.

findings.title: Service-address form covers multiple parties but has a single signature block
findings.evidence: Sample A lists the plaintiff and two defendants, but the form has one '确认人：' signature block; the second defendant has no address.
findings.recommended_action: Provide per-party confirmation/signature blocks or separate forms; do not treat one party's address as another's; record the source of each service address.

known_legal_questions: Whether the correct official counterpart is a generic lease dispute, a residential lease dispute, a commercial lease dispute, or a separate variant.
Whether the product should remain a lessor-only arrears template or also support a lessee plaintiff claiming delivery of the premises or return of the deposit.
Whether the plaintiff's right to rent or authority to sublease must be captured and reviewed before asserting a rent claim.
Whether the complaint should request termination, confirm an already-completed termination, or remain silent on contract status in each procedural posture.
Whether arrears, late fees, deposit set-off, occupation-use fees and damages must be separated into distinct claims.
Whether demand/notice, termination notice, return of premises and the date of actual return require separate user-confirmed fields.
Which court has jurisdiction when the property location, defendant residence and contractual jurisdiction clause differ.
Whether an official standalone evidence-list or service-address confirmation form exists for rental disputes.
